title: Lights in clubs, Preservation Hall travels and the dark 25
summary: Asked about flashing lights, Punch says the darkest place he knew was the 25.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Did you ever talk to the Preserv... Huh? Did you ever talk to Billy and Didi or any of the musicians who played at the Fillmore or any of those? What Billy?
The musicians, you ever talk to the guys at Preservation Hall, all the musicians, about all their travels when they go up to New York and...
Play with the lights? Yeah, I didn't know all about that. Do they, do they like those flashing lights?
No. They like all those lights when they play? Yeah. They got all kind of funny colored lights and that and everything, huh?
They didn't have that here, you see. Never have, huh?

No, no. The darkest place I went in here was way back there at 25 when I went in... at 25 where Lewiston was from. You could dark, damn light. You could hardly see it there. Well, that darkest place I don't remember.
It was dark when I went there.
It was dark the last time I was there. Yeah. It still wasn't there all that light. But did they have candles or regular electric light bulbs?
Not yet. Dun, dun, dun, dun.
